questions.heading: A Quality Gate Runs Every Rule After the Schema and Before the Model
questions.stem: A new export passes the snapshot schema: every field has its type and bounds, and every parent id names a project. A planner asks whether it is now safe to solve. What does passing the schema establish?

options.text: That the model has a plan, though it may not be the best one
options.says: Passing the schema does not give a plan at all: the lesson's parent cycle and lag typo both passed it.

options.text: That the plan will be right, though it may take long to solve
options.says: Budgets in millions are within their bounds (non-negative integers) and still wrong.

options.text: That the model can be built, though its data may still be wrong
options.says: Right: the schema settles that the model can be built; the gate asks whether the data is worth solving.

options.text: Little, since the gate may repeat the checks the schema makes
options.says: The gate assumes a valid snapshot and adds rules the schema cannot express; it repeats none of them.

questions.heading: Rules Across Projects Catch Errors No Single Field Shows
questions.stem: An export makes two optional projects each the other's parent, one with a lag of one year. Neither is must-do, and nothing else is wrong. What does the solver return for this snapshot?

options.text: An optimal plan that funds neither project, with no sign of the error
options.says: Right: funding neither satisfies every row, so the solver returns OPTIMAL with both quietly gone.

options.text: Infeasible, since the two projects' precedence rows contradict each other
options.says: The rows only force both projects to zero, which is allowed for optional projects; the lesson's run was OPTIMAL.

options.text: An optimal plan that funds both projects, since each one's parent is in it
options.says: With a lag, each needs the other to start strictly earlier, which no pair of years allows.

options.text: An error from the model build, since a project cannot be its own ancestor
options.says: The model builds without complaint; only the gate's cycle rule names the problem.

questions.heading: Severity Follows What a Finding Proves: Errors Block, Warnings Report
questions.stem: A rule flags each year whose budget moved by more than a factor of 3 since the last accepted snapshot. This cycle one year's budget quadrupled, and no other rule fires. Which severity should this rule have?

options.text: Error, since a change that large is almost always a typo in the export
options.says: A new program can raise a budget that much; blocking would refuse a real decision.

options.text: Error, since a plan solved from a budget like that cannot be trusted
options.says: An error must prove a broken contract or no plan; a large change proves neither.

options.text: Warning, since the solver will refuse the snapshot anyway if it is wrong
options.says: A wrong budget can still solve: the lesson notes that a fivefold budget passes every sound rule.

options.text: Warning, since a large change can be real and the rule cannot tell which
options.says: Right: the rule cannot tell a real change from a typo, so it reports and lets the sound rules block.
